text.p: Gasoline edged down on Tuesday as sellers outweighed buyers with the 95-octane breaking through the $23.00-mark, traders said.
A Japanese trader bought 50,000-barrels of 95-octane at $22.80 per barrel, fob Singapore, lifting Septmber 12-16 from a Swiss trader, they said.
The grade was offered on Monday at $23.00 but last traded at the end of July at $23.80.
Other than a blip in late July, 95-octane was last assessed below $23 in September.
But traders assessed overall fundamentals as balanced with the high-octane "still quite bullish" while the lower octane grades in good supply.
Unleaded 97-octane was offered by a Japanese trader at $24.35 or $1.55 higher than the traded 95-octane and the 92-octane was offered 30 cents lower but was later withdrawn by a U.S. major.
"The 92/95-octane spread is narrowing again," a trader said. "But realistically it should be around 60 cents."
Naphtha held steady, ignoring the marginal gains in crude.
Both September and October were last quoted at $21.00/$21.10 per barrel, unchanged from Monday.
At market close, October Brent on IPE last traded at $19.02 per barrel, up nine cents after from London overnight saw a six cent fall to close at $18.93.
"The market is very soft, and there are good avails, but nobody is offering cargoes because there is no demand," said a naphtha buyer.
He said both Singapore and Mideast cargoes were available for September, with some term lifters asking for swaps for later October liftings amid high stocks in North Asia.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
